cards.explanation: The answer is all the words of this law. Moses says, “Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over to enter the land…” (Deuteronomy 27:3). Not a few favorites, not a highlights reel. ALL the words of this law, on big plastered stones, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, “You must not use any iron tool on them.” (Deuteronomy 27:5). Then he repeats it: the altar of the LORD goes up with uncut stones (Deuteronomy 27:6). So no iron tools on those stones, friends. They go up just as they are.

The answer is rejoice. Moses says they're to sacrifice peace offerings, “…eating them and rejoicing in the presence of the LORD your God.” So this altar isn't only burnt offerings. There's eating and there's rejoicing, right there in front of the LORD. I'd show up early for that one, bakers.

The answer is to be silent and listen. Moses and the Levitical priests say, “Be silent, O Israel, and listen!” Before anything else gets said, the whole crowd has to get quiet. Some of us need that instruction at a family dinner, too, friends.

The answer is people. Moses and the priests say, “This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.” That's a big announcement to make out loud, bakers. They are His people, and they're told so right there.

The answer is True. Right after calling them the LORD's people, Moses and the priests say, “You shall therefore obey the voice of the LORD your God and follow His commandments and statutes I am giving you today.” That little word “therefore” connects the two, friends. They are His people, so they listen to His voice.

The answer is to bless the people. Moses says these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim “…to bless the people…” (Deuteronomy 27:12). He names six: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin. Not a bad assignment to get, bakers.

The answer is True. Moses says, “And these tribes shall stand on Mount Ebal to deliver the curse…” Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali are the six, friends. Gerizim handles the blessing and Ebal handles the curse.
The answer is Amen. After each curse, the text says, “And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’” The Levites speak and then everybody answers, friends. That's the whole crowd agreeing out loud.
The answer is dishonoring them. The curse says, “Cursed is he who dishonors his father or mother.” It's about how a man treats them, friends. And the people are to answer, “Amen!”

The answer is moves. The curse says, “Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.” (Deuteronomy 27:17). A boundary stone marks where a neighbor's land is, bakers. Moving it is the thing that gets named. And all the people say, “Amen!”

The answer is that he lets him wander in the road. Look at the verb in that curse, friends. It isn't about pushing him or tripping him. The curse lands on the man who “…lets a blind man wander in the road.” (Deuteronomy 27:18). So letting it happen is what gets named. It's like seeing a friend about to send a message to the wrong group chat and just letting it go through.

The answer is justice, and the verb matters just as much: “withholds.” The curse is on the one who holds justice back from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow (Deuteronomy 27:19). Nothing here says he took anything, friends. He kept it from them. And after each curse in this list, all the people are to say, “Amen!”
The answer is False. The final curse says, “Cursed is he who does not put the words of this law into practice.” It doesn't single out the priests, friends. And all the people answer, “Amen!”
